test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 16 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In 2025, which ministry of the Government of India organised Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan for ranking air quality in Indian cities?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Environment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan** is an initiative by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** to rank cities on the basis of air quality and the implementation of activities approved under the city action plan.
 
• The primary objective of the survey is to rank **131 non-attainment cities** in the country that have consistently failed to meet the National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for **five consecutive years**.
 
• For the year **2025**, the ministry continues to use this ranking system to foster a spirit of healthy competition among cities and encourage them to take proactive measures to reduce **air pollution**.
 
• The ranking is based on the **self-assessment** of cities on the **PRANA** (Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities) portal, where cities report their progress on **eight thematic areas**.
 
• These thematic areas include **biomass and municipal solid waste burning**, **road dust**, **dust from construction and demolition waste**, **vehicular emissions**, **industrial emissions**, **public awareness**, and **improvements in PM10 concentrations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP):**
 
 
• Launched in **January 2019**, the **NCAP** is a long-term, time-bound, national-level strategy to tackle the air pollution problem across the country.
 
• The programme initially aimed for a **20% to 30% reduction** in **PM2.5 and PM10** concentrations by **2024**, keeping **2017** as the base year for comparison.
 
• The goal was later updated to achieve a **40% reduction** in particulate matter concentrations by the year **2026**.
 
 
 
• **City Categories:**
 
 
• Cities are classified into three categories for the survey based on their population as per the **2011 Census**.
 
• **Category 1:** Cities with a population of **more than 10 Lakh** (over 47 cities).
 
• **Category 2:** Cities with a population between **3 Lakh to 10 Lakh** (44 cities).
 
• **Category 3:** Cities with a population **less than 3 Lakh** (40 cities).
 
 
 
• **International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies:**
 
 
• The awards for the best-performing cities under the **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan** are typically presented on **September 7th**, which is observed globally as the **International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies**.
 
• This day was designated by the **United Nations General Assembly** in **2019** to emphasize the need for further efforts to improve air quality to protect human health.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of CPCB:** The **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** plays a technical role in overseeing the air quality monitoring data and assisting the **Ministry of Environment** in the verification of city reports.
 
• **PRANA Portal:** The **PRANA** portal serves as a digital platform for monitoring the implementation of **NCAP**. It provides real-time information on the air quality status of **non-attainment cities** and tracks the progress of various mitigation activities.
 
• **Difference from AQI:** While the **Air Quality Index (AQI)** provides a real-time daily measurement of air health, the **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan** is a comprehensive annual ranking based on **policy implementation** and **long-term improvements** in air quality parameters.
 
• **Incentives:** The top-performing cities in each category receive **cash awards** and trophies to support further environmental conservation initiatives, funded by the **Government of India**.
